rubric_items.reason: All eight acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-14; out-of-scope items carry reasons.
Compound ACs split well into atomic REQs; REQ-3 bundles five row fields and REQ-14 'unchanged' is broad but still checkable.
Every known REQ cites the ticket line or an IDE answer (A-01..A-04) that says what the artifact claims; nothing invented.
No silent ticket/baseline clash; the booked-status question was asked (A-02), but its possible gap with the baseline booking rule is marked 'No mismatch' unverified.
Four questions, each with real options, answered by the engineer; none left open or blocking needlessly.
Plain and readable; glossary terms used consistently, though 'day schedule' and 'department' are used without a glossary entry or a found:false note.

findings.text: A-02 is recorded as 'No mismatch', but REQ-4 accepts whatever statuses the day schedule code counts, while the baseline says only Scheduled appointments block a slot. If the code counts Completed or No-show, the difference goes unrecorded.

cites.quote: options: Same as day schedule code (proposed default) | Scheduled only | Scheduled, Completed, No-show

findings.suggested_fix: Check which statuses GET /api/doctors/:id/slots treats as booked and record a mismatch on A-02 if it differs from the baseline Scheduled-only rule.

findings.text: The glossary check lists only terms that were found. It leaves out 'day schedule' and 'department', which the REQs use but the glossary does not define.

cites.quote: Each row shows the doctor's name, `department`, booked slots

findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Day schedule' and 'Department' to the glossary list with found: false.
